title: Provocative
slide_intent: Teach writers to decide when a challenge serves the reader and the purpose of the piece. A direct challenge needs a concrete issue and a way forward.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can name a harmful practice or power structure directly while giving an audience a reason and opportunity to act.
demonstration: The fifth principle weighs disruption against audience receptiveness. Its writing notes pair a challenge with evidence and a proposed solution.
practical_value: Name the specific practice that should change. Choose the level of confrontation for the audience and accompany the challenge with a possible response.

content_islands.name: Principle identifier
content_islands.spec: Mark Provocative in the chapter rail. Pair the large pale numeral 5 with its pink nameplate and the cyan underline.

content_islands.name: Definition and limits
content_islands.spec: Give the central column sufficient depth for the additional paragraph about when provocation could undermine the message.

content_islands.name: Writing guidance
content_islands.spec: Stack the practices at right. Include the example of confronting inaction, the guidance on varying tone and the requirement to offer a solution.
